prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK Manifesto (2024), policy-focused and non-ideological

Core aims
- Freeze non-essential immigration; end small-boat crossings via detain-and-deport policies and, if needed, returns to France; target zero NHS waiting lists; raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; reduce energy bills by scrapping Net Zero and expanding domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential visas (healthcare as main exception).
- Create a Department of Immigration; leave the ECHR; no UK resettlement for illegal entrants.
- Detain and rapidly process illegal arrivals, including offshore; bar asylum/citizenship for arrivals from safe countries; no legal aid for non-citizens; remove those refused.
- Immediate deportation of foreign criminals after sentences; allow citizenship removal for serious crimes.
- Bar student dependants; restrict post-study stays to essential skills; close fake courses.
- Five-year residency and employment requirement for benefits; clamp down on health tourism.
- Employer Immigration Tax: raise employer NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt essential health/care and very small firms).
- Claimed impact: savings £5–10bn pa plus £4bn pa revenue.

Public spending and regulation
- Stop Bank of England paying interest on QE reserves (claim: save ~£35bn pa).
- Reduce departmental spend by 5% without cutting front-line services (claim: £50bn pa).
- Cut remaining EU-derived laws and other regulations; halve foreign aid (save £6bn).
- Improve HMRC tax collection.
- Claimed potential savings: £91bn pa.

Tax and personal finances
- Raise income tax start point to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000 (cost: £70bn pa).
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; remove VAT and green levies from energy bills.
- Cut residential stamp duty: 0% to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% above.
- Reinstate VAT-free tourist shopping; reform inheritance tax: 0% up to £2m, 20% above (charity option).

Business and jobs
- No corporation tax on profits up to £100k; main rate 25%→20%, then 15% by year 3 (cost: £18bn pa).
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals.
- Planning reform to fast-track brownfield projects; reduce employment-law barriers to hiring/firing; simplify tax code.

NHS and social care
- Zero basic rate tax for NHS/social care front-line staff for 3 years; remove medical training caps; write off student fees over 10 years of NHS service.
- Use independent capacity in UK/overseas; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Voucher if GP wait >3 days, consultant >3 weeks, operation >9 weeks; weekend theatre use; review PFI; charge for no-shows.
- Public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.
- Cost: £17bn pa. Social care: launch Royal Commission; tackle offshore tax structures in care.

Energy and environment
- Scrap Net Zero and related subsidies/mandates (claimed public-sector saving: £30bn pa).
- Fast-track North Sea oil/gas and shale test sites; advance SMRs, gas turbines, synthetic fuels, tidal.
- Scrap £10bn pa renewable subsidies via equivalent taxes on them.

Policing and justice
- Recruit 40,000 officers to reach 300 per 100k population; expand stop-and-search; tougher penalties including mandatory life for drug trafficking; new “substantial possession” offence.
- Preference for ex-military recruits; reduce non-operational roles; revise complaint oversight.
- Justice: increase budget from £10bn to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; build 10,000 detention places; sentencing reforms; grooming-gang and youth-offending measures.
- Costs: policing £3bn pa; justice £2bn pa.

Education and families
- Curriculum changes; restrictions on school gender policies; single-sex facilities; parental notification under 16.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; raise entry standards; expand Pupil Referral Units; two-year degree options.
- Family measures: proposed transferable marriage allowance; front-load child benefit ages 1–4; single-sex public facilities; review online safety/social media.
- Cost: education £5bn pa; families £8bn pa.

Housing and infrastructure
- Fast-track brownfield housing; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; drop Renters (Reform) Bill; strengthen leaseholder protections.
- Scrap HS2 (one-off saving £25bn); ban ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; focus transport on regions; new utility ownership model: 50% public/50% UK pension funds; cap standing charges; consolidate infrastructure funding.
- Ongoing savings: £5bn pa.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farming budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked subsidies with direct payments; reduce red tape.
- Tighten access to UK waters; licence fees for foreign vessels; expand enforcement; ban foreign supertrawlers; rebuild UK processing and fleets.
- Costs: agriculture £2bn pa; fisheries £2bn pa.

Brexit, defence, and governance
- Repeal retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; review EU cooperation.
- Defence: spending to 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; veterans department; procurement reform; recruit 30,000 (cost £14bn pa).
- Constitutional changes: leave ECHR; reform Lords/civil service; restrict postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Additional proposals on media regulation, public holidays, anti-corruption unit.

Funding overview (party estimates)
- Claimed annual savings/growth: ~£160bn pa; total new costs: ~£141bn pa.
